_safe: A copy of this file names nothing to contact until you fill it in: "camera_ip" is empty, so a run over the network stops and asks for it (with CAMSET_USB=1 the kit connects over USB instead), and "readers" lists none, so a run that asks a reader (the crawl, the proofs, the walks) stops before it presses anything and says so. Put your camera's address in "camera_ip", and copy the readers you choose from "readers_examples" into "readers" (docs/QUICKSTART.md, step 3).
_camera: Which camera the kit works on; its runs go to runs/<model>_fw<firmware>/. With one camera nothing is needed: kit/tools/identify.py --camera starts its folder, and the kit takes the one camera in runs/; or name it, "camera": "<model>_fw<firmware>" as identify.py prints it. With more than one, "cameras" lists them, each {"model", "firmware"} with its own camera_ip, camera_model, hdmi or eyes where they differ, and "camera" names the one in use. --camera <model>_fw<firmware> or CAMSET_CAMERA on a command overrides it. "cameras_example" is not read by the kit (docs/QUICKSTART.md, step 3).
_comment: "readers_examples" is not read by the kit: copy the entries you choose into "readers" (docs/QUICKSTART.md, "Choosing a reader"). "vllm" and "omlx" are the two this project used (a server on the network and one on the Mac itself), at example addresses: put your own server's in "url"; Ollama, OpenAI and Gemini are untested here, and their "model" is a placeholder for a vision model that server or service offers. "api_key_env" names the environment variable holding a hosted service's key; the key itself never goes in this file.

readers_examples.name: ollama
readers_examples.model: a vision model you have pulled

readers_examples.model: a vision model the service offers
